checks_run.procedure: F-DG7-940: run the shipped tests on the unmodified tree, then apply authorization mutants one at a time and run ONLY export-scope.test.ts. M4 (required by the assignment) removes the scoped authorize() from requireExportRight. M6, M7 and M8 each drop one route's requireExportRight. M9 drops the create pre-check.
checks_run.environment: $TMPDIR/rv at 471072d64, Node 24.21.0, tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh (disposable PostgreSQL 16.15, port 32462), vitest --configLoader runner --project integration
checks_run.expected: The controls pass. M4 makes export-scope.test.ts fail. The sources are restored byte-equal afterwards.
checks_run.actual:
R0: export-scope.test.ts 4/4 and export.test.ts 10/10 pass, exit 0.
M4: 3 of 4 tests fail, exit 1. The ADM_TECH @ business_unit and @ transformation tests fail at l.169 (the six operations are no longer all 403). The audit-trail test fails at l.184 (extra audit events by narrow principals). The org-scope control passes. The mutant is KILLED.
M6 (list), M7 (get) and M8 (both manifest downloads): each is killed with 3 of 4 failing, exit 1. The failure is 'contract: … does not declare status 500'. The platform's fail-closed response guard (apps/api/src/modules/platform/hooks.ts:5-6) replaces a response from a route that never consulted the policy with a 500, so dropping a route check fails closed rather than leaking data.
M9 (create pre-check dropped): survives, 4/4 pass, exit 0. This is expected and not a gap: requestExport re-checks the right inside its transaction (service.ts:160), so the narrow principals still get 403 and no row, outbox event or audit event is written.
The sha256 sums of service.ts and routes.ts are equal before and after the mutants. Every exit 1 in this log belongs to a mutant run, as designed; there are no other failures.

checks_run.procedure: F-DG7-960/920: run a fresh protocol audit on THIS candidate (--stage DG7 and --all). Compare the C3 hits with REQ-DLV-012, release-notes.md and known-limitations.md. Run release-notes --check, known-limitations --check and check-handover (default and strict). Revert-to-fail with the round-3 handover files.
checks_run.command: node tools/release/protocol-audit.mjs --stage DG7 --root . --json $TMPDIR/pa-dg7.json; node tools/release/protocol-audit.mjs --all …; static-sec.sh (20-f920-f960-handover.log part)

checks_run.expected: Every surface states seven C3 hits, all seven named, matching the fresh audit; the --check commands exit 0; the round-3 files revert-to-fail.
checks_run.actual:
protocol-audit --stage DG7 exits 1 by design (hits present): 35 hits, C2 27, C3 7, C5 1. C1, C4, C6, C7, C8 and C9 PASS.
The C3 hits are AN-P7B, ARCH-R2, ARCH-R5, BE-R5, DO-A2, DO-D8 and FE-C3, out of 77 implementation handbacks. AN-P7G and BE-R8 have all the sections.
REQ-DLV-012 names all seven. Release notes l.35 says 'seven: the five D-270 hits plus F-DG7-960's FE-C3 and F-DG7-920's DO-D8 handback'. Known-limitations l.62 shows DG7 C3 HIT 7.
--all exits 1 by design: 281 hits in 29 checks, 0 blocked. Its status and hit count per (check, stage) equal protocol-audit-r4.json, so the table matches this candidate.
release-notes --check exit 0; known-limitations --check exit 0; check-handover exit 0 in both modes. The round-3 release notes and known-limitations each revert-to-fail with exit 1, as expected.
The orchestrator's prefreeze-r4/checks.log has two 'find: The -delete action automatically turns on -depth' warnings from its cleanup step (no effect on the checks), and runs the protocol audit with '; true' because the hits exit 1 by design.
I judge the hits themselves as disclosed deviations (D-249/D-270 user decision), not as met.

Run an independent probe of the candidate's stop/restart sequence against a real PostgreSQL 16, with the pre-DO-D8 sequence as a negative control. Run the drill's own test file under with-pg.sh.
checks_run.command: bash …/scripts/f921-restart-probe.sh; node --test deploy/scripts/tests/transfer-drill.test.mjs (first without, then under tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh)
checks_run.environment: $TMPDIR/rv at 471072d64, Node 24.21.0, PostgreSQL 16.15 (/usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin), probe ports 32490-32491, with-pg port 32462
checks_run.expected: The candidate sequence starts a new postmaster and the data persists. The disclosure about the earlier runs is correct. The drill tests pass.
checks_run.actual:
git log shows deploy/scripts/transfer-drill.sh and drill/cleanup.sh last changed in 7c819f08c (DO-D8B), so the cited t-b11-run.log describes the shipped code. Its D9 line, job-check PASS, equal export and download SHA-256, mode 2 reconcile and 'D9 PASS in 9.573 s' are as AN-P7G states. There is no 'did not stop before its restart' line.
Probe P1 (candidate sequence): old postmaster 38 gone, new postmaster 128, later pg_postmaster_start_time, persisted row 42. Result: real restart.
Probe P2 (pre-fix stop_pid, SIGTERM to the launcher, as in f8f86a78d l.122-127/592): old postmaster 244 still alive with the same start time. Result: no restart. This confirms the disclosure about the DO-D7, DO-E and QA-C runs. P2 omits stop_pid's later SIGKILL to the launcher, which cannot reach the postmaster either. No postgres server was left afterwards.
The first drill-test run (34-drill-tests.log) exited 1. The T-B3, T-B10 (x2), T-B16, T-B17 and T-B19 suites failed in under 1 ms because I ran the file without a database. The re-run under with-pg.sh, as the orchestrator runs it, passes 55/55 with 0 fail and 0 skipped, exit 0 (34b). That includes the real-PostgreSQL td_stop_pg and td_stop_pg_dir cases.
The 'FAIL status / deeplink / downloads / gatechain' lines in 34b are child output of negative tests that require those failures (wrong origin expectation, empty inbox, no download list, T-B18 missing remedy). Their tests pass.

checks_run.procedure: Inspect the P7 security surfaces on this candidate directly: the export authorization path (requireExportRight, all route call sites, the platform response guard), the new test's assertions, and the OIDC loopback exception (D-258). Confirm by diff that the other P7 surfaces inspected in round 3 have not changed since then.
checks_run.command: grep/sed over apps/api/src/modules/transfer/export/{service,routes}.ts, apps/api/src/modules/platform/hooks.ts, packages/config/src/load.ts; git diff --stat 8323dacae..471072d6 -- . ':!docs'

requireExportRight (service.ts:142-147) admits only on authorize(…, MIGRATION_EXPORT, {type:'organization'}). It is called on list (routes.ts:94), create (107, and again inside the transaction at service.ts:160 under an advisory lock), get (132) and both downloads (141). Each route also declares config.access, and the hooks.ts response guard fails closed.

The source diff since round 3 is only the new test (10-static.log). checks_run.procedure: Run the required validators on the live repository: --historical for DG6 down to DG1, --stage DG7, --pipeline and --register DG7. Compare stages.json at the source commit and at the freeze commit.
checks_run.environment: Live repository, read-only, HEAD a76c2aed4, Node 24.21.0
checks_run.expected: The assignment says '--historical --stage DG6 must pass (and DG5…DG1)'. --register passes. --stage DG7 fails only because the gate record and the round-4 reviews are missing, which is expected before the audit.
checks_run.actual:
All six --historical runs (DG6, DG5, DG4, DG3, DG2, DG1) print 'FAIL … (1 problem) - stages.json: DG7 illegal transition REVIEWING -> REVIEWING', exit 1. --pipeline gives the same single problem, exit 1. --stage DG7 gives the same problem plus the expected 'gate DG7: file not found', exit 1. --register DG7 PASS, exit 0.
Cause: the freeze commit a76c2aed4 appended {REVIEWING, 2026-11-16T03:55:37Z, 'Round 4 frozen…'} directly after round 3's REVIEWING entry, with no FIXING entry for the round-3 FAIL. rules.mjs TRANSITIONS allows REVIEWING -> FIXING|VERIFYING|BLOCKED only.
At the source commit the history still ended FIXING -> REVIEWING, which is why prefreeze-r4/historical.log passed: it ran before the freeze.
Raised as F-DG7-941 (Medium, not mandatory, owner delivery-orchestrator), the same class as F-DG4-104/124 and F-DG6-911/951. It is metadata only and does not change the candidate, but the gate cannot validate until it is fixed.

The candidate at HEAD 8d1ba28af is still sha256:d91f7152…0e59 over 3155 files, exit 0. git status shows only run directories and evidence, plus the other reviewers' files, which I did not open.

summary: Verdict FAIL. Of the four round-3 findings, F-DG7-940 (mutant M4 now killed by the shipped test), F-DG7-960, F-DG7-920 (seven C3 hits on every surface, matching a fresh audit) and F-DG7-921 (the cited DO-D8B run really restarts PostgreSQL; independent probe with a negative control) are CLOSED_VERIFIED on candidate d91f7152. The round-4 source delta is one test file, and I found no security defect in the code. T-A11, the real built-SPA/runtime/config asset scan that pre-freeze skipped, ran and passes. One new Medium finding, F-DG7-941: the round-4 freeze commit records DG7 REVIEWING -> REVIEWING in stages.json, so every required --historical validation (DG6..DG1), --pipeline and --stage DG7 exit 1. The fix is a metadata-only correction by the delivery-orchestrator that does not change the candidate; it must be repaired before the gate (D-192). No business, Finance, IT or production approval is granted or implied, and product G6 does not imply DG7.
